{"task":{"id":"Prob154_fsm_ps2data","spec":"
I would like you to implement a module named TopModule with the following
interface. All input and output ports are one bit unless otherwise
specified.

 - input  clk
 - input  reset
 - input  in (8 bits)
 - output out_bytes (24 bits)
 - output done

The module should implement a finite state machine that will search for
message boundaries when given an input byte stream. The algorithm we'll
use is to discard bytes until we see one with in[3]=1. We then assume
that this is byte 1 of a message, and signal the receipt of a message
once all 3 bytes have been received (done). The FSM should signal done in
the cycle immediately after the third byte of each message was
successfully received.

Implement the datapath module that will output the 24-bit (3 byte)
message whenever a packet is received (out_bytes[23:16] is the first
byte, out_bytes[15:8] is the second byte, etc.). The reset signal is
active high synchronous. out_bytes needs to be valid whenever the done
signal is asserted. You may output anything at other times (i.e.,
don't-care). Assume all sequential logic is triggered on the positive
edge of the clock.

Here is an example waveform:

  time   clk rst in  done out_bytes
  0ns    0   1    0  x         x
  5ns    1   1    0  0         x
  10ns   0   1    0  0         x
  15ns   1   0   2c  0         x
  20ns   0   0   2c  0         x
  25ns   1   0   81  0         x
  30ns   0   0   81  0         x
  35ns   1   0    9  0         x
  40ns   0   0    9  0         x
  45ns   1   0   6b  1    2c8109
  50ns   0   0   6b  1    2c8109
  55ns   1   0    d  0         x
  60ns   0   0    d  0         x
  65ns   1   0   8d  0         x
  70ns   0   0   8d  0         x
  75ns   1   0   6d  1    6b0d8d
  80ns   0   0   6d  1    6b0d8d
  85ns   1   0   12  0         x
  90ns   0   0   12  0         x
  95ns   1   0    1  0         x
  100ns  0   0    1  0         x
  105ns  1   0    d  1    6d1201
  110ns  0   0    d  1    6d1201
  115ns  1   0   76  0         x
  120ns  0   0   76  0         x
  125ns  1   0   3d  0         x
  130ns  0   0   3d  0         x

Inline all helper logic inside TopModule; do not define auxiliary modules. xczu3eg-sbva484-1-e; 5 ns synthesis clock; simulator seed 1. No reference dependencies, hierarchy outside the DUT, file access, includes or DPI."},"current":{"revision_id":"d0cc5ece-00bd-465e-9d36-7e9c6fc4ddcf","source_sha256":"988cc80b3a1aeb666d63b9656e3f96f98649d1367e000527eb41a1df6382bc2e","source":"module TopModule (
    input  logic        clk,
    input  logic        reset,
    input  logic [7:0]  in,
    output logic [23:0] out_bytes,
    output logic        done
);

    typedef enum logic [1:0] {
        SEEK = 2'd0,  // discarding bytes, looking for a start byte (in[3]=1)
        GOT1 = 2'd1,  // received byte 1, waiting for byte 2
        GOT2 = 2'd2,  // received bytes 1-2, waiting for byte 3
        DONE = 2'd3   // received all 3 bytes; report the message
    } state_t;

    state_t     state, next;
    logic [7:0] b1, b2;

    // Next-state decode (combinational)
    always_comb begin
        case (state)
            SEEK: next = in[3] ? GOT1 : SEEK;
            GOT1: next = GOT2;
            GOT2: next = DONE;
            DONE: next = in[3] ? GOT1 : SEEK;
            default: next = SEEK;
        endcase
    end

    // Sequential datapath. done and out_bytes are registered on the
    // transition INTO DONE, so they are valid during the very next cycle
    // (the cycle immediately after the third byte was received).
    always_ff @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state     <= SEEK;
            done      <= 1'b0;
            out_bytes <= 24'h000000;
            b1        <= 8'h00;
            b2        <= 8'h00;
        end else begin
            state <= next;
            done  <= (next == DONE);

            case (next)
                GOT1: b1 <= in;                  // capture byte 1
                GOT2: b2 <= in;                  // capture byte 2
                DONE: out_bytes <= {b1, b2, in}; // capture byte 3, form message
                default: ;
            endcase
        end
    end

endmodule

I found the defect: `done` (and `out_bytes`) are registered from the current state, so they assert one cycle **later** than required. The spec requires `done` in the cycle immediately after the third byte. I'll derive `done` from the *next* state and register `out_bytes` at the transition into the done state.
messages.reasoning_content: Now edit with the corrected design. The bug: done/out_bytes asserted one cycle late. Fix by computing done from next state and registering out_bytes when next==DONE.
